name: Feedback harness hook
purpose: The single hook handler for both Claude Code and Codex, exposing the quiet rule as a pure function and the per-harness output shape as a thin wrapper.
responsibilities: Read harness JSON from stdin (session_id, cwd, hook_event_name, stop_hook_active, last_assistant_message) and never block longer than 1 second
Apply the quiet rule (design section 3.5) and return ask or silent
Emit the exit-2-plus-stderr shape for Claude Code and the JSON block shape for Codex
Install itself under .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json via a mergeable installer that never clobbers other hooks
Report missing-hook and foreign-hook conditions to doctor and repair missing hooks under --fix
internalStructure: src/feedback/hook.js exports shouldAsk(state) -> "ask"|"silent" (pure) and emit(harness, decision, entries) (side-effect). src/setup/feedback-hooks.js merges the entries into .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json; doctor reuses the installer helpers for the report.

interfaces.name: shouldAsk
interfaces.description: Pure decision on the quiet rule; unit-tested across the full table.

interfaces.name: emit
interfaces.description: Per-harness output; exit code and shape.

interfaces.name: installHooks
interfaces.description: Merge the hook entries into the two harness config files.

dependencies.name: TAC-4102-feedback-store
dependencies.description: Read state and settings; write the asked ledger.

tradeoffs: Two harness config files to maintain and one handler; the cost is small (one merge pattern per file) and the benefit is one implementation of the quiet rule for both harnesses.
notes: The asked record is appended before the emit path, so a crash between emit and reply cannot cause a second ask.
